Subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation — ACME POC follow-up

Kyle — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we can size the Dedicated POC and validate SLOs.

Recap (from call):
- Target latency SLO: p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 250ms for streaming responses (chat).
- Expected steady-state concurrency: ~60 concurrent users during peak, spiking to ~80 for short bursts.
- Typical prompt size: ~120 tokens input, ~250 tokens output on average.
- Streaming required: yes — low-latency partial token delivery is important for UX.

What we need from you to finalize test plan:
1) Confirm p95/p99 targets above (or provide different numbers).
2) Confirm peak concurrency and expected sustained RPS / tokens/sec during peak (approx).
3) Any max per-chunk latency threshold for streaming (e.g., <100ms per chunk)?
4) Sample prompt set (or a synthetic distribution) we can use for POC.

Proposed Redwood POC plan (attached as acme_poc_test_plan.pdf):
- Phase A (baseline): run open-model variant on A10G-equivalent to establish cost baseline + throughput.
- Phase B (SLO validation): run on A100 and H100 profiles with int8 quant and mixed precision to measure p95/p99 and streaming chunk latencies.
- Phase C (reserved throughput): provision dedicated capacity equivalent to tested throughput (we'll propose reserved RPS & concurrency based on Phase B results).

Preliminary sizing notes (high level):
- For your target above, we'd expect to recommend a reserved throughput bucket in the 80–150 rps range depending on batching and quantization.
- If you need hard p99 < 200ms with streaming, H100-class instances are likely required for peak concurrency.

Attachments: acme_poc_test_plan.pdf (test steps), gpu_comparison_table.xlsx (blank for us to populate after initial runs).

Next steps: if you confirm the SLOs & concurrency, we'll schedule the POC kickoff (30–60m) and block engineering time next week to run a baseline test.

Thanks, Rafael — that matches my notes. A few clarifications:

- Concurrency: sustained ~60 concurrent chat sessions, yes. Peak bursts up to ~85 for a few minutes.
- RPS / tokens: average combined throughput during peak ~120 requests per second, average output tokens ~250 per request.
- Streaming: yes — streaming chunks roughly every 100 tokens; we would like chunk latency <120ms ideally.

I'll attach a sample prompt set after I scrub PII (we have a few internal logs I can share).

1) Can you provide an initial recommendation for reserved throughput (rps) and GPU class for our target p95 100ms?
2) Can Redwood run an initial baseline on our synthetic prompt distribution without us providing real data? We'd prefer to get a directional recommendation first.

Kyle — quick technical take from infra/benchmarks (high level) given targets you shared. I'm summarizing expected behavior per GPU class for chat-style streaming workloads (int8 quant where supported):

Summary (approximate expected p95/p99 latencies at ~60 concurrent sessions, avg prompt 120 in / 250 out):
- A10G-equivalent (consumer class / cost-optimized): p95 ~ 220–300ms, p99 ~ 450–700ms — not likely to meet p95=100ms. Good baseline for cost comparison.
- A100 40GB: p95 ~ 110–160ms, p99 ~ 240–360ms at concurrency 60 with int8 and small batching. Could meet p95 ~100ms in tuned configs but risk at spikes.
- H100 80GB: p95 ~ 70–110ms, p99 ~ 140–220ms at concurrency 60 with int8/mixed precision — best chance to comfortably meet p95=100ms and keep p99 under 250ms at peak.

Reserved throughput (recommended starting buckets for POC):
- Baseline bucket: 100 rps (to cover average + buffer).
- Burst capacity: ability to scale to 150–180 rps during peak bursts via autoscale or reserved burst.

Streaming considerations:
- Chunk frequency: if you stream every ~100 tokens, network + model kernel latency per chunk needs to be <120ms to meet UX target. H100 provides best margin.
- Batching: continuous batching helps throughput but increases tail latency; for chat UX we keep micro-batch sizes small (batch size 1–8) and favor low-latency exec paths.

Actionable ask: Rafael / Marissa — we'll prepare a quick benchmark matrix for A10G / A100 / H100 (attached as gpu_comparison_table.xlsx) using your synthetic prompt set. Kyle — if you can share the synthetic distribution, we can run baseline tests without production data.

—Aditya
